answer: Agents mapping a willow grove, knoll or rocky ledge could qualify for rewards by maintaining a separate storage replica per earning key. Validators assign uniquely encoded data and demand proofs of random bytes before tight deadlines; failed audits suspend rewards. One copied proof cannot serve two keys. Each added alias therefore needs more disk space and audit bandwidth, even in parallel. This assumes sound encoding and deadlines that prevent regeneration; outsourcing still costs money, colluding farms still need capacity, and newcomers need storage.
